description.value: A longitudinal clinical and volumetric MRI study assessed annualized brain atrophy, ventricular expansion, and behavioral change in patients with frontotemporal lobar degeneration and age-matched healthy controls over approximately one year.

spans.text: Whole brain atrophy, ventricular expansion, and change in standard cognitive and behavioral indices were measured over a 1-year follow-up period in each of the major FTLD syndromic subgroups.

description.value: Longitudinal observational cohort study with assessments at baseline and one year later.

spans.text: Thirty-two patients with FTLD (11 behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia [bvFTD], 11 semantic dementia [SemD], 10 progressive nonfluent aphasia [PNFA]) and 24 age-matched healthy controls were assessed using volumetric brain MRI and standard behavioral measures (Mini-Mental State Examination, Frontal Assessment Battery, Clinical Dementia Rating Scale, Neuropsychiatric Inventory with Caregiver Distress scale) at baseline and 1 year later.

Sixty-two consecutive patients fulfilling current consensus criteria for FTLD2 attending the Cognitive Disorders Clinic at the National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, London, UK, between 2005 and 2008 were assessed for eligibility.
The FTLD cohort eligible to enter the study comprised 43 patients representing each of the 3 canonical clinical syndromes: bvFTD (n = 22), SemD (n = 11), and PNFA (n = 10).

name.value: Relationships between longitudinal MRI and cognitive measures

spans.text: Relationships between longitudinal MRI and cognitive measures were investigated for the entire FTLD cohort and for each patient subgroup.

definition.value: Associations between rates of whole brain and ventricular MRI change and changes in behavioral measures were investigated.

value: Decline in Mini-Mental State Examination score at 1 year was associated with increased whole brain atrophy rates for the FTLD cohort as a whole and the bvFTD subgroup, and with increased ventricular expansion rates in the language variant subgroups (SemD and PNFA). Deterioration in CDR-SB score was associated with higher rates of whole brain atrophy and ventricular enlargement for the FTLD cohort as a whole and for the bvFTD subgroup. Other relations between MRI and behavioral change measures were less consistent.
